arm: cheribsd-purecap, default async revocation, quarantine disposition only
what_this_bundle_is: NOT a verdict. The verdicts are in results/20261006-cheribsd. This bundle asks why cheribsd-revocation is silent on this group's eight misses: 3, 9, 10 and 17, whose object is a buffer the SYSTEM allocator handed out; 4, 5 and 8, whose object is a GC object slot inside an mrb_heap_page; and 13, which is spatial and frees nothing (declared not-temporal against the 2026-10-06 bundle). Case 2 is in the table because it was run, not because it needed answering: that arm CATCHES it.
answer: Two different answers in one program, one binary, one boot. 3, 9, 10, 17: QUARANTINED-UNSWEPT. 4, 5, 8: NEVER-FREED. Both from the same counters, told apart by who allocated the object.
how_measured: ports/common/host/cheribsd/quarantine-probe.c, sha256 fa283f7686c36e1803910e006dc429577ee132fd6eea12ef49a89b6b97263554, linked into the interpreter with -Wl,--wrap=malloc,--wrap=calloc,--wrap=realloc,--wrap=free. The wrap form exists because this arm's binary must be STATIC -- dynamically linked it dies in the loader with 'Traditional TLS not supported' -- and LD_PRELOAD does not reach a static binary. The probe reads the kernel's revocation shadow bitmap (one bit per 16-byte granule, set while quarantined) and the dequeue epoch from CHERI_REVOKE_SHADOW_INFO_STRUCT, whose advance counts completed sweeps. Nothing forces a sweep.
why_the_sweep_counter_decides_it: Without it the reading is unusable. With sweeps=0, memory freed during the case is never cleared, so a stale read succeeds WITHOUT the block being handed out again -- and then reused_while_quarantined=0 is uninformative about whether the object was in the quarantine. The argument recorded for Perl on 2026-10-06, that a zero in that column leaves only 'never entered the quarantine', assumed a sweep could have intervened. Under sweeps=0 it cannot, so that argument is weaker than it was written to be: see the correction in ../../../../perl/release-differential/results/20261006-cheribsd/inputs.json. What still separates the two silences is the program's own account of where its memory goes -- for memcached, four libc frees in the whole process; for mruby, nineteen hundred.

controls.the_sweep_counter_is_live: control:sweep churns 400,811 allocations through the same interpreter and reports sweeps=22, while control:no-sweep does almost nothing and reports 0. So a zero is a measurement and not a dead counter. Without this pair the whole bundle would be unreadable.
controls.the_interpreter_still_interprets: control:eval evaluates 6*7 to 42 with the probe on every malloc, free and realloc of a static binary.
controls.recursion_survives: control:recursion runs 500 frames and returns 500. This is the control the 2026-10-06 arm needed: without app patch 0010 this arm dies at about 40 frames under revocation, before reaching any case.
controls.the_platform_controls_passed: cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds, both PASS. A dynamic revocation-control in the same boot faulted at its labelled load, signal=34 code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG), so revocation is live in this boot.
controls.what_the_dynamic_control_does_NOT_show: its own QUARANTINE line comes from the supervisor process, not from the control: the control dies on SIGPROT and its destructor never runs. It is a control for revocation, not for the counters.

the_probe_perturbs_the_heap_so_this_run_: case 10 printed 'NOT_FALSE true' four times here where the 2026-10-06 arm records it completing with PASS. Wrapping every allocator call changes sizes and addresses, and whether a use-after-free reads the old or the new contents turns on exactly that. So no verdict is read from here -- only the disposition counters, and even those as the state of the mechanism rather than the fate of a particular block. The verdicts stay in results/20261006-cheribsd.
every_free_is_still_not_the_instrument: _RUNTIME_REVOCATION_EVERY_FREE_ENABLE=1 does make case 17 fault, and the 2026-10-06 README cited that as proof the block was quarantined and unswept. The conclusion happens to be right, but the argument is not usable: on perl the same configuration faults on a case that is an in-bounds read of a live object, which no mechanism may legitimately catch. The bitmap and the epoch establish it without that.
what_the_counters_can_and_cannot_do: They are PROCESS-WIDE. They establish the state of the mechanism, not the fate of one object: that every free lands in the quarantine (1229 to 1994 a case, all of them) and that no sweep ever completes (sweeps=0, against 22 under the churn control). They cannot say which block the stale pointer referred to. All seven readable cases therefore have the SAME counter shape, and attributing a case to one disposition or the other needs one more fact, which is declared and not measured here: who allocated the object. That is the corpus's allocator_boundary, from each case's allocator_layer.

how_the_two_are_told_apart.3, 9, 10, 17 -- quarantined-unswept: the object is a malloc'd buffer (the format String's buffer, the shaped-IV block, the struct's member storage, the key array's storage) and mruby frees straight through libc. So it entered the quarantine, and with sweeps=0 it was never cleared: the stale capability stayed valid. 3 and 9 read the old contents back intact and the harness reports PASS, which is what a read of quarantined-but-untouched memory looks like; 10 and 17 report wrong answers. Either way the mechanism had the object and the asynchronous window lost the race.
how_the_two_are_told_apart.4, 5, 8 -- never-freed: the object is a GC object slot inside an mrb_heap_page the system allocator still holds, so no free ever reaches the slot. The run shows this from the other side: all three print visibly CORRUPTED strings, with a run of raw bytes replacing the middle of a string literal the case had stored, so the memory was certainly handed out again, while reused_while_quarantined stayed 0, which says libc reissued nothing that was still quarantined. The reuse was mruby's own, inside a page libc never got back. Same argument as memcached's eight, reached from a different direction.
how_the_two_are_told_apart.2 -- not a question: case 2 is a CheriBSD CATCH in results/20261006-cheribsd, and it faults here too (exit 162, 'In-address space security exception'), so the two runs agree. It was put in this run by mistake, on a misreading of the miss list, and its row is kept with no counters because a faulting process runs no destructor. Nothing about it is evidence for or against a disposition.
